name: John S. Warn
role: Oyster Grotto restaurant proprietor; author of Lost Cabin mines series
bio: John S. Warn ran a Medora eating place the paper called his "temperance tabernacle" and the "Oyster Grotto," and he took part in the Republican county convention of August 1884 and the school meeting that December. From February to May 1885 he was held up in Bozeman, which the paper said was to settle an estate and wait for court; in April word came that he had been sentenced to a year in the penitentiary, and Medora people signed a petition for his pardon, calling the charges trivial and the work of enemies, though it turned out he had been sentenced to only thirty days. He returned in May 1885 and that June and July the Cow Boy ran his serial history of the Lost Cabin gold mines, as told to him by his uncle, Allen Hulburt. In late June 1885 he sold his restaurant to M. W. McDonald and left for Miles City to organize a search for the mines, and by early July he had bought the Commercial house hotel in Glendive.
